stem: One of the assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases is that all collisions involving molecules of the gas are elastic.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by an *elastic* collision.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State two other assumptions of the kinetic theory of gases.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A molecule of an ideal gas has mass *m* and is contained in a cubic box of side length *L*. The molecule is moving with velocity *u* towards the face of the box that is shaded in Fig. 3.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The molecule collides elastically with the shaded face and the face opposite to it alternately.

Deduce expressions, in terms of *m*, *u* and *L*, for:
parts.text: the magnitude of the change in momentum of the molecule on colliding with a face

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the time between consecutive collisions of the molecule with the shaded face

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: the average force exerted by the molecule on the shaded face

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: the pressure on the shaded face if the force in (iii) is exerted over the whole area of the face.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
When the model described in (b) is extended to three dimensions, and to a gas containing *N* molecules, each of mass *m*, travelling with mean-square speed ⟨*c*²⟩, it can be shown that

*pV* = ⅓ *Nm*⟨*c*²⟩

where *p* is the pressure exerted by the gas and *V* is the volume of the gas.

Use this expression, together with the equation of state of an ideal gas, to show that the average translational kinetic energy *E*ₖ of a molecule of an ideal gas is given by

*E*ₖ = ⅗ *kT*

where *T* is the thermodynamic temperature of the gas and *k* is the Boltzmann constant.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The mass of a hydrogen molecule is 3.34 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.

Use the expression for *E*ₖ in (c) to determine the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) speed of a molecule of hydrogen gas at 25 °C.

figures.caption: Fig. 3.1
figures.alt: A molecule moves inside a cube towards a shaded face, with the cube side labelled L and the molecule's velocity labelled u.

notes: In (c), the printed equation for average translational kinetic energy appears to be Eₖ = ⅔kT, not ⅗kT.
